title: In-memory rate limiting is per process, resets on restart and does not send Retry-After

original_titles.title: Rate limiting is in-process/in-memory and 429s lack a Retry-After header
In-process rate limiter resets on restart and multiplies per worker
Rate limiting is a per-process in-memory bucket
Rate limits: in-memory per-process only, several rows missing, values deviate
In-process rate limiter: per-worker limits, restart resets, unbounded key growth
429 responses lack Retry-After header (ERC-02 S1-part, ATH-01c)
429s carry no Retry-After header; rate limiter is in-process
Invalid callable annotations and unbounded rate-limit bucket keys
Rate limiting is in-process only; concurrency cap is dead config
Rate limiter is in-process only, resets on restart, and never evicts keys

problem: deps.rate_limit stores timestamp arrays in a process-local defaultdict. It resets on restart, is multiplied by worker/replica count and retains arbitrary keys. AUTH_RATE_LIMITED maps to 429 but the error handler does not add Retry-After.
impact: Attackers can evade limits by hitting another worker or waiting for restart, and clients cannot reliably respect the server retry window. The bucket dictionary can grow with unbounded distinct keys.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Move rate-limit counters to a shared atomic store such as Redis or PostgreSQL. Use atomic increment/expiry or a token-bucket script so simultaneous requests cannot exceed the limit.
Define limits by identity, IP, route class and account; bound the key cardinality and use privacy-safe hashed identifiers where appropriate.
Return Retry-After and structured retry seconds for every 429 response; standardize the policy across login, step-up, uploads, repository search, flags and submissions.
Add tests for concurrency, restart/reconnect, multi-worker behavior, expiry, spoofed headers and distinct-key floods.

acceptance_criteria: The same quota is enforced across two API processes.
Restarting a worker does not reset rate limits.
All 429s contain a valid Retry-After header and stable error code.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
